reigns.tagline: The teenage queen who gave her name to an age
reigns.cameToPower: Uncle died a month after she turned 18
reigns.previously: William IV dies at Windsor, having lived just long enough.
paragraphs: Victoria grew up under her mother's thumb at Kensington, never allowed to sleep alone or walk downstairs without holding someone's hand. Becoming queen set her free. Her first act was to move her bed out of her mother's room. In 1840 she married her German cousin Albert. She adored him. They had nine children and married them off across Europe, which is why she's called the grandmother of Europe.

Albert died in December 1861, aged 42, and Victoria fell apart. She wore black for the rest of her life and hid from the public for years. People grumbled. Then Disraeli coaxed her back, and in 1876 Parliament made her Empress of India. By her jubilees in 1887 and 1897 she was a national icon at the head of a vast empire.

She reigned for 63 years and 7 months, a record until Elizabeth II broke it. Victoria died at Osborne on the Isle of Wight in January 1901, aged 81. Her son was 59 and had been waiting his whole life.

claims.text: Victoria once said 'We are not amused.'
claims.note: It first appears in a 1919 book of gossip, long after her death. Her granddaughter Princess Alice said she never said it, and her letters show plenty of laughing.

claims.text: She used chloroform when giving birth to Prince Leopold in 1853.
claims.note: Her doctor John Snow gave it to her, and she praised the 'blessed chloroform' in her journal. It helped make pain relief respectable.

claims.text: Lesbianism was never made illegal because Victoria refused to believe women did such things.
claims.note: No evidence at all. The 1885 law only ever dealt with men, and the story surfaces many decades later.

reigns.hook: The old queen is dead. Her son Bertie, the playboy prince she never trusted, is finally king at 59, and the royal house now takes his father's German name.

reigns.tagline: The playboy prince who waited 59 years
reigns.previously: Victoria dies at Osborne after 63 years on the throne.
paragraphs: Bertie was a disappointment to his parents from the start. In 1861 news got out that an actress had been smuggled into his army camp in Ireland. Albert went to tell him off and died a few weeks later. Victoria blamed her son and kept him away from real work for forty years. So he ate, smoked, raced horses, shot birds and had a long line of mistresses, including Lillie Langtry and Alice Keppel.

His coronation in June 1902 had to be postponed two days before, when he needed emergency surgery on his appendix. It was a close thing. Once crowned, he turned out to be good at the job. He charmed Paris in 1903 and helped bring about the Entente Cordiale with France in 1904. He brought colour back to court after his mother's long gloom.
He also smoked a dozen cigars a day. In May 1910 he caught bronchitis and had a run of heart attacks. He died at Buckingham Palace after nine years as king. His son George took over.

claims.text: Victoria blamed Bertie for his father's death.
claims.note: Her letters say so. Albert had travelled to see Bertie about the actress scandal just before he fell ill.

claims.text: Alice Keppel, his mistress, was let in to say goodbye at his deathbed.
claims.note: Queen Alexandra allowed it. Alice Keppel is also the great-grandmother of Queen Camilla.

claims.text: His last words were that he was very glad his horse had won at Kempton that afternoon.
claims.note: The horse, Witch of the Air, did win and he was told. The neat last line comes from the court's own account.

reigns.hook: Edward VII is dead. His son George V takes the throne in 1910. Within four years Europe is at war, and the enemy is led by George's own cousin, the Kaiser.

reigns.tagline: The stamp-collecting king who invented the Windsors
reigns.cameToPower: Father died; elder brother died in 1892
reigns.previously: Edward VII dies at Buckingham Palace after nine years as king.
paragraphs: George was a navy man who never expected to rule. Then his elder brother Eddy died of flu in 1892. George took his place as heir and, a year later, married Eddy's fiancée, Princess Mary of Teck. He was gruff, punctual and obsessed with his stamp collection. He liked shooting at Sandringham far more than palaces.

His reign was a storm. The First World War set him against his cousins, the Kaiser and the Tsar. In 1917, with anti-German feeling running high, he swapped the family name Saxe-Coburg and Gotha for Windsor. That same year he backed out of giving the Tsar's family a refuge in Britain, and they were later shot by the Bolsheviks. In 1932 he made the first royal Christmas broadcast on the radio.

In January 1936 he lay dying at Sandringham. His doctor, Lord Dawson, gave him lethal injections of morphine and cocaine so he would die in time for the morning papers. His eldest son, a glamorous bachelor, became king.

claims.text: His doctor deliberately ended his life with injections.
claims.note: Lord Dawson's own notes, made public in 1986, describe giving morphine and cocaine so the death could be announced in The Times.

claims.text: He pushed for the British offer of asylum to Tsar Nicholas II to be withdrawn.
claims.note: Letters from his private secretary in 1917 show the king worried about the backlash at home.

claims.text: His last words were 'Bugger Bognor.'
claims.note: A much-loved story about his seaside recovery in 1929, but nobody can show he said it on his deathbed.

reigns.hook: George V is dead. His son Edward is 41, handsome, hugely popular and still unmarried. He is in love with an American, and she is married to someone else.

reigns.tagline: The king who gave up the throne for love
reigns.previously: George V dies at Sandringham, hurried along by his own doctor.
paragraphs: As Prince of Wales, Edward was a celebrity. He toured the empire, wore sharp suits and danced in nightclubs. His father despaired of him. By the time he became king he was in love with Wallis Simpson, an American who had divorced once and was in the middle of divorcing her second husband.

The government, the Church of England and the dominions all said a king could not marry her. Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin made it clear: Wallis or the throne. Edward chose Wallis. He signed his abdication on 10 December 1936 and the next night told the country on the radio that he couldn't go on 'without the help and support of the woman I love'. He was never crowned.

He became Duke of Windsor and married Wallis in France in 1937. That autumn the couple visited Nazi Germany and met Hitler. In the war he was packed off to govern the Bahamas, then spent the rest of his life in exile in France. He died in Paris in 1972.

claims.text: He told the nation he couldn't be king 'without the help and support of the woman I love'.
claims.note: It was a live radio broadcast on 11 December 1936, recorded and printed at the time.

claims.text: He and Wallis met Hitler in 1937.
claims.note: Photographs and newsreels show the visit to Germany in October 1937.

claims.text: In 1940 the Nazis plotted to keep him in Europe as a puppet king, and he went along with it.
claims.note: Captured German files show the plot was real. How much Edward knew or encouraged it is still argued over.

reigns.hook: Edward is gone. His shy younger brother Bertie, who has a stammer and never wanted the job, is suddenly king, with a wife and two small daughters.

reigns.tagline: The reluctant king with a stammer and a war to win
reigns.reignEnded: Died in his sleep at Sandringham
reigns.previously: Edward VIII abdicates to marry Wallis Simpson.
paragraphs: Albert, known as Bertie, was shy, sickly and had a bad stammer. He served at sea and fought at the Battle of Jutland in 1916. From 1926 an Australian speech therapist, Lionel Logue, helped him get his words out. He married Lady Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon in 1923, and they had two daughters, Elizabeth and Margaret. He took the name George to show the country nothing had changed.

Less than three years after his crowning, Britain was at war with Germany. The king and queen stayed in London through the Blitz. Buckingham Palace was bombed in 1940, and the queen said she was glad, because now she could look the East End in the face. He created the George Cross for civilian bravery and gave it to the whole island of Malta in 1942.

After the war India became independent and he stopped being Emperor. A heavy smoker, he had lung cancer and had a lung removed in 1951. On 6 February 1952 he died in his sleep at Sandringham, aged 56. His daughter was on the other side of the world.

claims.text: Lionel Logue helped him manage his stammer, including before major broadcasts.
claims.note: Logue's own diaries and letters, published by his grandson in 2010, back this up.

claims.text: The queen said the princesses would not leave without her, she would not leave the king, and the king would never leave.
claims.note: Her famous answer when it was suggested the family move to Canada for safety, widely reported in 1940.

claims.text: Elizabeth climbed up a tree a princess and came down a queen.
claims.note: The line was written by hunter Jim Corbett at the Treetops lodge in Kenya. Nobody knows the exact hour the king died, so she may already have left.

reigns.hook: In Kenya, a 25-year-old princess hears that her father is dead. She flies home as Queen Elizabeth II, and she will reign for seventy years.

reigns.tagline: Seventy years, fifteen prime ministers, one queen
reigns.cameToPower: Father died while she was in Kenya
reigns.previously: George VI dies in his sleep at Sandringham, aged 56.
paragraphs: Elizabeth was born third in line and was never meant to be queen until her uncle abdicated. In the war she joined the ATS and trained as a driver and mechanic. On her 21st birthday she promised on the radio that her whole life would be devoted to service. Later that year she married Philip Mountbatten. They had four children: Charles, Anne, Andrew and Edward.

Her coronation in June 1953 was shown on television, and millions crowded round borrowed sets to watch. She saw the empire turn into the Commonwealth and worked with fifteen British prime ministers, from Churchill to Truss. She had hard years too. In 1992, which she called her annus horribilis, three of her children's marriages broke down and Windsor Castle caught fire.

She celebrated her Platinum Jubilee in June 2022, the first British monarch to reach seventy years on the throne. On 6 September she appointed Liz Truss at Balmoral. Two days later she died there, aged 96. Her eldest son, heir for seventy years, was finally king.

claims.text: She worked with fifteen British prime ministers.
claims.note: From Winston Churchill in 1952 to Liz Truss in 2022, all on the public record.

claims.text: She sent her first email in 1976.
claims.note: She sent it over ARPANET, an early forerunner of the internet, during a visit to a defence research centre in Malvern.

claims.text: She trained as a mechanic during the Second World War.
claims.note: She joined the Auxiliary Territorial Service in 1945 and learned to drive and repair army lorries.

reigns.tagline: The longest apprenticeship in royal history
reigns.previously: Elizabeth II dies at Balmoral after seventy years on the throne.
paragraphs: Charles became heir at the age of three and waited longer than anyone in British history. He was made Prince of Wales in a ceremony at Caernarfon Castle in 1969 and took a degree at Cambridge. In 1976 he set up the Prince's Trust to help young people, and he spent decades speaking up for the environment, organic farming and traditional architecture.

He married Lady Diana Spencer in 1981 and they had two sons, William and Harry. The marriage broke down and they divorced in 1996. Diana was killed in a car crash in Paris the next year. In 2005 Charles married Camilla Parker Bowles, who is now Queen Camilla.

He was crowned at Westminster Abbey on 6 May 2023. In February 2024 the palace announced that he was being treated for cancer, and he carried on with state business. His heir is his elder son, William, Prince of Wales. This story is still being written.

claims.text: At 73, he was the oldest person to become British monarch.
claims.note: The previous record holder was William IV, who was 64 when he took the throne in 1830.

claims.text: He is the longest-serving heir apparent in British history.
claims.note: He was heir for over seventy years, from 1952 to 2022, passing Edward VII's record in 2011.

claims.text: He was the first heir to the British throne to earn a university degree.
claims.note: He graduated from Trinity College, Cambridge, in 1970.
